alternate_names: Swayambu Sidhpeeth Sri Gupteshwar Mahadev Mandir
deities: Parvati (separate temple opposite, joined by gathbandhan on Maha Shivratri)

history.summary: An ancient Shiva temple on the Gupteshwar hills on the banks of the Narmada in Jabalpur, styled 'Swayambu Sidhpeeth'. Tradition (Shiva Purana's Koti Rudra Samhita, Ramayana, Skanda Purana) holds that Lord Rama fashioned the Shivling out of sand during a secret (gupt) stay at Tripuri Tirtha while searching for Sita, performing abhisheka with Narmada water and tapas for a month alongside Lakshmana and Rishi Jabali; the linga is called an upling (sub-linga) of Rameshwaram Jyotirlinga. The shrine was long hidden - a boulder blocked the cave mouth - and was rediscovered around 1890. Note the Rama-made legend sits uneasily with the 'swayambhu' (self-manifested) epithet (verify). A Maa Parvati temple stands opposite, with a gathbandhan of the two dhwajas on Maha Shivratri.

name: Sri Gupteshwar Mahadev Mandir
town_description: Jabalpur is a major city of Madhya Pradesh on the Narmada, a cantonment and rail hub best known for the marble-rock gorge and Dhuandhar Falls at Bhedaghat and for Kalachuri-era antiquity. The Gupteshwar locality, on Kailashpuri Road southwest of the city centre, holds this cave/shrine Shiva temple among several other ancient tirthas on the river.

travel.railway: Jabalpur Junction - approx 7-8 km (verify); Madan Mahal station nearer (verify)
travel.road: On Gupteshwar Main Road / Kailashpuri Road, Gupteshwar, southwest of Jabalpur city centre; reachable by auto and taxi (verify)
